events.name: Quantum Computing Symposium: Latest Advances in Quantum Algorithms
events.description: Join leading researchers from Columbia's Quantum Computing Lab for presentations on the latest breakthroughs in quantum algorithms, hardware development, and practical applications. Topics include Shor's algorithm implementations, quantum error correction, and industrial applications in cryptography and materials science.

events.name: Medieval Literature in the Digital Age: New Critical Approaches
events.description: An interdisciplinary conference exploring medieval texts through modern critical lenses. Featuring presentations from scholars across multiple disciplines including digital humanities, comparative literature, and medieval studies. Topics range from digital manuscript analysis to contemporary interpretations of medieval narratives.

venue.name: Bobst Library, Room 119
venue.address: 70 Washington Square S, New York, NY 10012

events.name: Climate Change Policy in the Urban Context: New York Case Studies
events.description: Panel discussion on international climate policy frameworks and their implementation at the local level, with a focus on New York City's sustainability initiatives. Featuring policymakers, environmental experts, and urban planners discussing carbon reduction strategies, green infrastructure, and climate adaptation policies.

events.name: Neuroscience Discovery Series: Brain-Computer Interfaces
events.description: Monthly lecture series highlighting cutting-edge research in brain function, neurological disorders, and cognitive neuroscience. This month's focus: emerging technologies in brain-computer interfaces, neural prosthetics, and the ethical implications of neurotechnology advancements.

events.name: Contemporary Art Exhibition: Digital Identity in the Metaverse
events.description: Opening reception for the annual MFA thesis exhibition featuring work from emerging artists exploring themes of identity, technology, and digital consciousness. The exhibition showcases multimedia installations, virtual reality experiences, and traditional media reimagined through digital perspectives.

events.name: Legal Ethics in the Digital Age: AI and Legal Practice
events.description: Panel discussion examining ethical challenges posed by emerging technologies in legal practice. Topics include artificial intelligence in legal research and decision-making, blockchain applications in contract law, data privacy regulations, and the evolving role of attorneys in digital society.

venue.name: Vanderbilt Hall, Room 204
venue.address: 40 Washington Square S, New York, NY 10012

events.name: Human-Computer Interaction: Designing for Accessibility
events.description: Workshop and panel discussion on designing technology interfaces that are accessible to users with diverse abilities and needs. Topics include universal design principles, assistive technologies, inclusive user research methods, and the business case for accessibility in tech development.

events.name: Urban Anthropology: City as Cultural Text
events.description: Lecture series exploring urban spaces as cultural artifacts and social texts. Drawing from anthropology, sociology, and cultural studies, this series examines how cities encode social relationships, power dynamics, and cultural identities through their physical and social landscapes.

events.name: Contemporary Music Performance: Experimental Techniques
events.description: Student recital featuring experimental music compositions and performance techniques. The program includes works that explore extended techniques, electronic integration, interdisciplinary collaboration, and new approaches to musical expression in the 21st century.

venue.name: Paul Recital Hall
venue.address: 60 Lincoln Center Plaza, New York, NY 10023

events.name: Astrophysics Seminar: Dark Matter and Galaxy Formation
events.description: Weekly seminar series featuring research presentations on astrophysical phenomena. This week's topic explores recent discoveries in dark matter distribution, galaxy formation theories, and the implications for our understanding of the universe's large-scale structure.
